searchText: Does the CI fill the tests? If yes, what EVM it uses? Is https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7610 accepted? This is already reported: https://github.com/ethereum/tests/issues/1368 ok. Can we have a separate folder for eof in execution-spec-tests? I'm diving into the `eofparse` parts of execution test spec, looking for ways to wire in Besu's and Geth's tools of choice. Would the testing team prefer - A stand-alone `eof-parse-tool` like `transition-tool` that auto detects from `--evm-bin` - Have the exiting client specific transition tools either return an `EOFParse` instance through a new method - Or should `verify_fixture` be plumbed through to support the tests? with the clients making appropriate chagnes to the CLI including possibly launchign a different tool? Do you mean like its own separate fork? So instead of `prague` -> `eof-fork` ? rather `prague/eof` Your convention is to group tests by eip, but we have ~10 EIPs for EOF and also it is not always possible to have a test that affects only single EIP. Could you expand on number 2? I don't quite understand how would that look So something like `prague/eof/eip3540_eof_v1` + `prague/eof/eip663_dupn`, and so on? sounds good to me, because otherwise the prague folder would become too crowded yes. <@403707149043105803> <@275684146658148352> <@425343240212971521> ok? > Tests: Included the type and version of evm t8n tool used to locally execute test cases: e.g., ref with commit hash or geth 1.13.1-stable-3f40e65. How to exactly do this? This is unnecessary since it's automatically added to the fixtures, we need to remove that checkmark It will make it clearer what the EOF and non EOF tests are.

I'm diving into the `eofparse` parts of execution test spec, looking for ways to wire in Besu's and Geth's tools of choice.  Would the testing team prefer 
- A stand-alone `eof-parse-tool` like `transition-tool` that auto detects from `--evm-bin` 
- Have the exiting client specific transition tools either return an `EOFParse` instance through a new method
- Or should `verify_fixture` be plumbed through to support the tests? with the clients making appropriate chagnes to the CLI including possibly launchign a different tool?
